speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in. To better understand your chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination, I need to ask a few questions. Have you noticed any blood in your urine, pain during urination, or fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pain relief after voiding and the recent painful intercourse are significant findings; do you also feel a deep pressure or fullness in your lower abdomen when you are not urinating?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome.

The combination of chronic bladder pain relieved by voiding, significant urinary frequency, and dyspareunia in a 40-year-old female strongly points to this diagnosis, as the symptoms have persisted for five months despite NSAID use.
